subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Check Valves: One-Way Flow
description: A short lesson to help you apply Check Valves: One-Way Flow.

hook.text: A check valve lets fluid flow in one direction only. Reverse flow pushes a ball or poppet onto its seat.

buildup.text: Spring pressure keeps the valve closed. Forward flow must exceed the cracking pressure to push it open.

discovery.text: Pilot-operated check valves can be overridden by a pressure signal. This lets you unlock a cylinder when needed.

twist.text: Without check valves, a hydraulic cylinder holding a load would slowly sink as oil leaked back through the circuit.

climax.text: Check valves protect pumps from backflow, hold loads overhead, and isolate circuit branches. Tiny but essential.

punchline.text: One direction only. The simplest rule, enforced by a ball and a spring.

quiz.question: Why are pilot-operated check valves used with hydraulic cylinders?
options: They allow the cylinder to extend faster by bypassing the pump
They lock the cylinder in position but can be overridden when needed to lower the load
They filter contamination from the oil before it enters the cylinder
